skill.name: salesforce-title-refresh
skill.description: Check Salesforce contact titles and seniority with Leadsets. Review proposed updates for contacts at the same company and flag possible company moves in a dated change log.
skill.summary: Review Salesforce title and seniority changes, flag company moves, and keep a dated record of each check.
skill.author: leadsets

security_audit.summary: The command execution and reconnaissance alerts are false positives, and the homepage and signup URLs are documentation links. The Leadsets connection sends contact identifiers to an external service, and review-first mode saves identifiable logs before Salesforce approval. Same-company matching lacks a required per-contact identity, freshness, or confidence check before updates; no evidence of prompt injection was found.

remediation.issue: Salesforce contact identifiers are sent to Leadsets.
remediation.suggestion: Before enrichment, confirm that the organization permits sending the selected identifiers to Leadsets. Send only the identifier needed for each lookup.

remediation.issue: Identifiable change logs are saved before Salesforce write approval.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the log destination and access permissions before saving. Default to restricted storage and omit contact identifiers that are not needed for review or reconciliation.

remediation.issue: Same-company matches can be written without sufficient evidence about the person or role.
remediation.suggestion: Require a per-contact identity match, a recent checked date, and adequate confidence before any automatic update. Route ambiguous matches or missing evidence to manual review.

semantic_findings.title: Contact log is saved before Salesforce approval
semantic_findings.description: Review-first mode saves a CSV or named Google Sheet before Salesforce approval. The log contains contact names, Salesforce IDs, and employment details without a required access check.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill explicitly saves the full log before approval. Exposure depends on who can access the chosen file or sheet.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic updates lack per-contact verification gates
semantic_findings.description: Auto-write can update contacts based on a company-domain match after a single-contact probe. The workflow logs confidence and verification dates but sets no minimum confidence or freshness requirement.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The steps do not require a per-contact identity check before writing. A wrong person at the same company or an outdated role could pass the stated checks.

content.value_statement: Outdated job titles make it harder to route, score, and segment Salesforce contacts. Check current roles with Leadsets, review proposed updates, and flag contacts who may have changed companies.
actual_capabilities: Read contacts from a Salesforce report, list view, or filter, and remove duplicates by Salesforce ID and email.
Check Leadsets usage, test one contact lookup, and size batches to available enrichment records.
Compare current roles with Salesforce records and distinguish material changes from formatting differences.
Replace eligible titles and update an existing seniority field after approval, or use explicitly requested auto-write.
Flag company moves without updating those records, and count contacts with missing identifiers or no match.
Save a dated CSV or named Google Sheet with old values, new values, and the action taken.
limitations: Requires a Salesforce connection and either a Leadsets MCP connection or a Leadsets REST API key.
Requires a work email, a LinkedIn URL, or a name and company for each lookup. Leadsets may still return no match.
Does not create Salesforce fields, change accounts or owners, update email addresses, or start sequences.
Review-first mode delays Salesforce updates, not enrichment or saving the change log.

use_cases.title: Review seniority before scoring
use_cases.description: Check titles and seniority for a defined account group before running scoring rules. Review the proposed values before they affect routing.

use_cases.title: Check contacts before outreach
use_cases.description: Check contacts from a Salesforce list view before a new sales sequence. Review possible company moves separately instead of replacing those contact titles.

use_cases.title: Reconcile approved title updates
use_cases.description: Compare approved Salesforce updates with the dated change log. Use contact IDs and old and new values to verify the changes.

prompt_templates.title: Preview a first batch
prompt_templates.scenario: First review of a Salesforce contact list.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check up to 20 contacts from [Salesforce list view]. Show me proposed title changes and wait for approval before updating Salesforce.

prompt_templates.title: Review contacts at open accounts
prompt_templates.scenario: Contact review before a sales sequence.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review up to 100 contacts at accounts with open opportunities. Flag company moves separately, save a CSV, and wait for Salesforce write approval.

prompt_templates.title: Check an existing seniority field
prompt_templates.scenario: A targeted check of fields used for scoring.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check Title and [existing seniority field] for contacts in [Salesforce report]. Show old and new values and save the log to [restricted Google Sheet]. Wait for Salesforce write approval.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a quota-limited refresh
prompt_templates.scenario: A larger refresh that may span several usage windows.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check up to 500 contacts from [Salesforce report] whose titles have not changed in 180 days. Fit batches to current Leadsets limits and report when remaining contacts can resume. Flag company moves and wait for approval before updating Salesforce.

output_examples.input: Check 25 contacts from the renewal list and wait for approval.
output: Review ready: 5 proposed title changes, 2 possible company moves, 16 unchanged contacts, and 2 contacts with no match.
The dated CSV is saved. No Salesforce records were updated.

output_examples.input: Apply the six approved title and seniority changes. Keep company moves flagged.
output: Updated 6 approved Salesforce contacts. The 3 contacts flagged for company moves were not updated.
The change log records the old and new values, check dates, and actions taken.

best_practices: Start with a small report or list view. Confirm the first Leadsets result identifies the intended contact.
Use review-first mode and verify identity, company, and role freshness before approving each proposed update.
Confirm that Leadsets is approved for the contact data and restrict access to the CSV or Google Sheet.
anti_patterns: Assuming review-first mode prevents Leadsets lookups or stops the change log from being saved.
Approving a title update for a contact flagged as having changed companies.
Sending contact logs to a public or broadly shared spreadsheet.

faq.question: What connections do I need?
faq.answer: You need a Salesforce connection and a Leadsets account. Connect the Leadsets MCP server or supply a Leadsets REST API key through your approved setup.

faq.question: Which contacts are checked by default?
faq.answer: The default targets contacts whose Title has not changed in 180 days. It checks up to 500 contacts, subject to available Leadsets quota.

faq.question: Will it update Salesforce without approval?
faq.answer: Review-first mode waits for approval before updating Salesforce. If you request auto-write, eligible changes for contacts at the same company are written without a separate review.

faq.question: What happens when a contact changes companies?
faq.answer: The skill flags the contact in the change log. It does not replace that contact's title or change the Salesforce account.

faq.question: What if Salesforce has no seniority field?
faq.answer: The skill records inferred seniority in the change log without creating a Salesforce field.

faq.question: Where is the change log saved?
faq.answer: The default is a dated CSV. You can name a Google Sheet instead. The log is saved even when Salesforce updates are awaiting approval.
